values.note: All 20 sites book online through My County Parks. 1-night minimum, 3 nights on Memorial Day, 4th of July and Labor Day weekends. Reservations are final, with refunds only for listed emergencies, by calling the conservation office. Check-in after 3 pm, check-out before noon.

note: Floyd County Conservation park of 40 wooded acres along Ackley Creek, a mile southwest of Marble Rock, with two shelters, a playground and hiking trails. The camping loop sits in the woods with no view of the creek or the Shell Rock River, which is about 350 m northeast across fields. --Claude
summary: Confirmed $20 sites (20, with 30-amp electric and water), showers, dump, season (about May-October), online booking and the 14-night limit. Not waterfront stands. Pin on the loop.
flags: FIT: no lengths are posted. The site pages say '20 gravel campsites'. NAIP shows gravel back-in spurs off a small loop with trailers on them, so a 23-ft motorhome looks fine. No caveat proposed.

WATERFRONT: not waterfront confirmed. The loop is in the woods. Ackley Creek isn't visible on NAIP near the sites, and the Shell Rock River is about 350 m northeast, beyond the county road and fields. There is no view of either. The old note's 'set back from the Shell Rock River' is replaced: the park page places the park on Ackley Creek.
SEASON: the park page says 'approximately May through October'. The old note said ~May-Sept. No opens/closes dates are written because the page only gives approximate months.
PIN OK: 42.95320,-92.87480 sits on the camping loop. Phone OK: 641-756-3490 is the Floyd County Conservation office given on the site pages.
